MESSAGE:
Wedding planning question dump, apologies in advance!

Could you suggest a hashtag for our wedding? We're Priya and Tom. And I need a sentence for the invitation saying children are welcome at the ceremony but not at the evening reception, phrased kindly so nobody's offended. While you're at it, how should we word the RSVP deadline so people actually reply on time?

We're hiring a photo booth for the evening. The company charges £95 an hour plus a flat £60 setup fee, with a minimum booking of 3 hours. We want it running from the moment the wedding breakfast ends right through to the end of the party at midnight. What will the booth cost us in total?

Also, what colour should the bridesmaids wear for an October wedding in a barn? Our colours are sage and cream. Three ideas for favours that cost under £2 each, please, ideally not sugared almonds. And is a seating plan better as one big board by the door or as individual escort cards? We have about 90 guests for the meal, if that changes the answer.

Thank you!

RESPONSE:
# Wedding Q&A

## Hashtag ideas
- **#PriyaAndTomTieTheKnot**
- **#ThePriyaTomWedding** (simple, easy to remember)
- **#TomFoundHisPriya** (sweet and a bit playful)
- **#SagelyWed** (a nod to your sage colour scheme)

Search each one on Instagram first to make sure it isn't already in heavy use.

## Children at the ceremony only
> "We adore your little ones and would love them to join us as we say 'I do'. The evening reception will be an adults-only celebration, so we hope you can enjoy a well-deserved night out."

## RSVP wording
> "Please let us know by **[date]** whether you can join us. We need final numbers for our caterers, so we won't be able to hold a place after this date."

Set the printed deadline 2 to 3 weeks earlier than your real one, which gives you time to chase stragglers. Making it easy to reply (a QR code or website link) helps a lot too.

## Photo booth cost
You didn't mention what time the wedding breakfast ends, so I can't give one total. The formula is **(£95 × hours) + £60 setup**, with a 3-hour minimum:

| Breakfast ends | Hours | Total |
|---|---|---|
| 7:00pm | 5 | £535 |
| 8:00pm | 4 | £440 |
| 9:00pm | 3 | £345 |
| 9:30pm or later | 3 (minimum applies) | £345 |

If you tell me the time, I'll confirm the exact figure. If the breakfast runs late, you'd still pay for 3 hours, so you could start the booth a little before the party begins at no extra cost.

## Bridesmaid colour
Since sage is already one of your colours, I'd go for **sage dresses in a slightly deeper, olive-leaning shade**, which feels right for October. Cream bouquets with some rust or burnt-orange accents would suit the autumn barn setting. If you want variety, mixed shades of sage look lovely in photos.

## Favours under £2
1. **Mini jars of local honey or jam** with a sage-coloured tag (often £1.20 to £1.80 in bulk)
2. **Wildflower seed packets** ("Let love grow"), usually under £1
3. **Hot chocolate or mulled-spice sachets** in a small bag, which suit an October evening

## Seating plan
For 90 guests, I'd go with **one large board**, arranged alphabetically by surname with table numbers. It suits a barn look, costs less, and is quick to make. Place it away from the door, or split it into two panels, so people don't queue in the entrance. Choose **escort cards** only if you're assigning individual seats, since they take more time to set up and to find on the day.

Congratulations to you both!
